thread:
alex: Heads-up — APAC edge (rack-7 / eu2-equivalent) showing sustained p95 GPU latency spikes since 03:10 UTC. KV cache evictions up 7x. Suspect noisy tenant causing memory pressure.

maria: Saw it too. Which tenant? any correlation with dedicated pools?

alex: Metrics point to tenant 'stream-vids' on node rack-7a. They jumped batch size earlier at ~03:05 via rollout.

kevin: @maria @alex can we route new allocations off that rack? quick fix: soft-fallback to edge-reserve pool in next-closest AZ.

sre-bot: deploybot: rollback completed for rollout stream-vids v2 at 03:18 UTC.

maria: rollback helped but p99 still elevated. We're seeing cross-tenant PCIe saturation traces on that shelf.

jon: Proposal: carve a tiny fractional dedicated slice (2 GPUs) for latency-sensitive tenants in APAC edge to absorb noisy behavior during spikes.

anya: Cost question — fractional carveouts increase reserved capacity overhead. Rough estimate: +$1.2k/month for that tiny slice in prod.

kevin: If we do fractional slice, we need QoS-tagging + router preference so best-effort tenants still get routed elsewhere when warm pool is under pressure.

maria: Agreed. Also want a short-term network mitigation: limit jumbo-batch sizes from stream-vids at proxy layer. Quick patch idea: set per-tenant max_batch=32 for APAC for 1h.

alex: Patch applied (proxy config). Command run:
```
kubectl patch configmap proxy-config -n edge --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/tenants/stream-vids/max_batch","value":32}]'
```

alex: After patch, KV evictions down ~40% and latency trending down. Still watching.

jon: For medium-term: two options — 1) ephemeral fractional dedicated slice with auto-evacuate and preemptive fallback, or 2) stricter routing policy: prefer dedicated pools only for pinned tenants and route large-batch jobs to cooler AZs.

anya: We should include unit economics in the decision: fractional slice reduces tail latency but costs reservation overhead; routing prefers cooler AZs increases egress and cross-region cost and may violate data locality for some customers.

kevin: Takeaway: short-term proxy batch cap worked. Next steps: run a 72h experiment with 2-GPU fractional slice + QoS tags, measure p99, cost delta, and cross-AZ egress. If cost delta > $3k/month with <25% p99 improvement, revert to routing policy.

maria: I'll own the experiment. Plan: create slice, add routing tags, set canary for low-risk tenants, monitor via /dash/edge-apac/noise.

alex: Oncall will get alert if p99 > 250ms for 10m. @kevin please add runbook snippet for evacuation and preemptive drain.

kevin: Will do. Runbook snippet added to playbook repo and linked in #incidents.

sre-bot: monitor: noise-detector triggered on rack-7 at 03:49 UTC; assigned to @maria.

maria: Thanks. Will follow up with post-experiment summary in 72h. Short notes: shard-level KV cache tagging would help long term to avoid whole-rack fallout.

anya: Agreed on KV tagging; add to backlog and cost-compare with fractional slices.

alex: Closing loop — temporary mitigations working. Keep thread updates minimal unless p99 regresses. :thumbsup:
